systematic_read.airway_lungs: CURRENT: Trachea central, no narrowing seen. Lungs well expanded. No consolidation, mass or collapse. Linear bronchovascular markings are mildly prominent in the medial right lower zone, with a single small dense nodular focus projected among them. Left lung clear. Apices clear. PRIOR: Trachea central. Lungs expanded. No consolidation, mass or collapse. Right lower zone markings are less conspicuous on a softer exposure. Haziness over the left lower zone conforms to the overlying breast shadow.
systematic_read.mediastinum_hila: CURRENT: Prominent aortic knuckle. Upper mediastinum not widened. Hila normal in position, no one-sided hilar enlargement. PRIOR: Same prominent aortic knuckle and mediastinal contour. Hila similar.
systematic_read.pleura: CURRENT: No pleural line to suggest pneumothorax; markings reach the chest wall. Both costophrenic angles sharp. No pleural thickening. PRIOR: No pneumothorax. Right costophrenic angle sharp. Left costophrenic angle overlapped by breast shadow, without definite blunting.
systematic_read.heart: CURRENT: Heart not enlarged on PA view. Borders distinct. PRIOR: Heart not enlarged on PA view. Borders distinct. No change in size or contour.
systematic_read.diaphragm_below: CURRENT: Both domes well defined, right slightly higher than left. Gastric bubble and gas-filled bowel loops under the left dome. No free gas under the diaphragm. PRIOR: Domes well defined. Less bowel gas visible. No free gas.
systematic_read.bones_soft_tissue: CURRENT: No rib, clavicle or shoulder fracture or destructive lesion seen at this resolution. Visible spine aligned. Bilateral breast shadows. No soft tissue gas. PRIOR: Same appearance. Bilateral breast shadows, the left projecting lower and wider than on the current, likely positional.
systematic_read.devices: CURRENT: Thin tubing arcs across the left upper zone from the medial left clavicular region to a small metallic component over the lateral left upper to mid zone. Appearance is consistent with an implanted venous access port and catheter. Catheter tip not traced over the mediastinum. PRIOR: Same device, projected slightly lower over the left mid zone. No new device.

findings.description: Left chest tubing with a small metallic component, consistent with an implanted venous access port and catheter. Catheter arcs across the left upper zone toward the medial left clavicle. Tip not traced.
findings.evidence: Same device configuration on both studies. It projects higher on the current, in keeping with different arm and breast position. No kink or discontinuity seen at this resolution.

findings.description: Mildly prominent linear bronchovascular markings in the medial right lower zone on the current study, with a single small dense nodular focus projected among them. No confluent consolidation.
findings.evidence: Markings are more conspicuous on the current than on the prior. The current is slightly more penetrated with higher contrast, and this difference might explain the appearance. The small nodular focus is not clearly seen on the prior.

findings.description: Prominent rounded aortic knuckle, consistent with an unfolded aorta. Upper mediastinum not widened.
findings.evidence: Same contour and prominence of the aortic knuckle on both PA studies, with no rotation on either.

cant_determine.question: Is the small dense focus in the medial right lower zone a true lung nodule, and is it new?
cant_determine.reason: The focus is small and lies among vessels, so a vessel seen end-on or a calcified granuloma cannot be separated from a nodule on a frontal film. The softer exposure of the prior may hide it.
cant_determine.recommend: Review the source images in PACS. If it persists, CT chest.

cant_determine.question: Have the right lower zone lung markings truly increased since the prior?
cant_determine.reason: The current study is more penetrated with higher contrast, which makes fine markings more conspicuous without a real change.
cant_determine.recommend: Review source images side by side in PACS with matched windowing. Interval follow-up PA film, or CT chest if there is clinical concern.

cant_determine.question: Where is the tip of the left-sided venous catheter?
cant_determine.reason: The thin catheter cannot be followed over the dense mediastinal shadow on these low-resolution frontal images.
cant_determine.recommend: Review the source image in PACS with edge-enhanced windowing, or obtain a lateral view.

systematic_read.mediastinum_hila: CURRENT: Aortic knuckle prominent. Upper mediastinum not widened. Aortopulmonary window not filled in. systematic_read.diaphragm_below: CURRENT: Right dome slightly higher than left, both well defined. Gastric bubble under the left dome with several gas-filled bowel loops in the left upper abdomen. systematic_read.bones_soft_tissue: CURRENT: Mild curvature of the thoracic spine. No displaced rib fracture or destructive rib lesion at this resolution. Clavicles and shoulders intact. systematic_read.devices: CURRENT: Left chest wall venous access device with a small metallic component projecting over the left upper to mid zone. PRIOR: Same device, metallic component projecting slightly lower over the left mid zone with a similar catheter loop. No new device on the current study.

findings.description: Left chest wall venous access device with catheter looping toward the left subclavian region. Present on both studies. The metallic component projects higher relative to the ribs on current than on prior.
findings.evidence: Same device type and catheter loop on both films. The component projects over the left mid zone on prior and the left upper to mid zone on current. Arm, shoulder and breast position differ between the films and may account for the shift.

findings.evidence: Markings are clearly seen on current. On prior the same zone is covered by breast shadow and the film has lower contrast, so technique may explain the difference. No confluent consolidation on either film.

cant_determine.recommend: Review the source images in PACS. No further imaging needed if the radiologist confirms normal vessels.
